reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports graphene's high strength and its ability to increase strength in Cu/graphene composites, but it does not provide any evidence for graphene's thermal conductivity, its effect on interfacial thermal resistance, its bonding to tungsten, or its behavior under irradiation. Most key premises are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Graphene has exceptionally high intrinsic thermal conductivity
Graphene can form a coherent, well-bonded interlayer between W and Cu
The graphene interlayer reduces interfacial thermal resistance by facilitating electron and phonon transport
The graphene interlayer maintains mechanical integrity and mitigates defect propagation under irradiation
Graphene interfaces increase strength in metal/graphene composites (e.g., Cu/graphene)
